summary: Orangeburg County, SC tower near Bouchetts Cross Roads, built for the state forestry commission about 1940, replaced by steel in 1957-58; NHLR-registered 2016; condition not confirmed.

facts.status_note: NHLR registration (2016) gives no current condition; no source read says whether the tower still stands

staffing.status: once staffed by a lookout named Mildred Zeigler; no dates in the sources read

access.note: Administered by the South Carolina Forestry Commission; the sources read give no public visit information

visit.trail_note: No visit information found; ask the Forestry Commission before going to the site.

events.note: Report for the fiscal year July 1940 to June 1941 lists the Way Tower among three towers constructed that year
Buildings and fence at the site completed by CCC labor (report for 1941-42)
Report for 1957-58 says the old wooden tower was replaced by a new steel structure
Registered November 21, 2016; nominated by Terrie D. Johnson

evidence.supports: three towers constructed in the 1940-41 report year, one of them the Way Tower
evidence.quote: A total of three towers were constructed during the year. One of which the Way Tower near Bouchetts Cross Roads in Orangeburg County.

evidence.supports: the 1940-41 report window is July 1940 to June 1941
evidence.quote: Report of the State Commission of Forestry, 7/1/40 to 6/30/1941

evidence.supports: buildings and fence at the Way Tower completed by CCC labor in the 1941-42 report year
evidence.quote: The buildings and fence at the Way Tower, near Bouchetts Cross Roads in Orangeburg County, were completed by CCC labor.

evidence.supports: old wooden tower replaced by a new steel structure in 1957-58
evidence.quote: The old wooden tower located at Way was replaced by a new steel structure.

evidence.supports: protected Orangeburg County and was previously staffed by Mildred Zeigler
evidence.quote: This lookout protected Orangeburg County. It was previously staffed by a lookout named Mildred Zeigler.

evidence.supports: administered by the South Carolina Forestry Commission
the commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993
evidence.quote: The Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993.

corrections.why: The NHLR entry gives a 2016 registration and photos but no statement of current condition, and no page read says the tower still stands.

notes_for_editor: Build and replacement years are the fiscal-year report windows (FY 1940-41 and FY 1957-58), recorded as 1940 and 1957; the exact months are not in the sources. The history comes through Forest Lookouts' transcriptions of the commission's annual reports, not the originals. Status and access are unconfirmed. A social-media post in search results describes the site as overgrown, but its page could not be read, so it is not cited. Mildred Zeigler's dates are not given.
